source.note: R188. R186's ten losses are two disjoint families of five, and the aggregate now prints the split: five games act every turn and never find the object (49 or 50 environment steps, 0 or 1 thoughts), five spend the pass's fifty turns on thoughts and touch the world 4 to 26 times (24 to 46 thoughts). The separation holds on the winning side too -- no won game in 264 has twenty thoughts -- and the pack already moves the mean, 9.23 thoughts a game in the control to 4.2 with the scoped bank. So half the remaining gap is a turn-economy failure, not a search failure, and this entry is the direct instruction against it: a reply that only plans spends a turn and changes nothing.
operations_kept: one command per turn, on its own line (clean, cool, examine, heat, puttwo)
open the container before taking from it (put)
end every reply with a command rather than a plan (all six kinds)

entries.text: If a "put" action repeatedly fails despite being at the correct location and holding the object, try the alternative phrasing "move <object> to <receptacle>". Write the command alone on its own line and put nothing under it: a command that shares a line with a thought is read as part of the thought, so it never reaches the world and still costs a turn.

If a "put" action repeatedly fails despite being at the correct location and holding the object, try the alternative phrasing "move <object> to <receptacle>". A closed container hides its contents: open the cabinet, fridge, drawer or safe before taking anything from it, or the take answers "Nothing happens." and the put that follows fails the same way.
